research_topic: Can we predict the next pandemic?

accepted_gaps.title: Target conflation
accepted_gaps.statement: Spillover propensity, outbreak detection, spread escalation, and pandemic prediction are often conflated.

accepted_gaps.title: Stage attribution
accepted_gaps.statement: Existing risk products often do not identify the stage producing a high risk estimate.

accepted_gaps.title: Evaluation realism
accepted_gaps.statement: Temporal, geographic, delay-aware, and calibration evaluation is insufficiently standardized.

accepted_gaps.title: Decision linkage
accepted_gaps.statement: Risk ranks rarely define an accountable action, threshold, lead-time need, or false-alert cost.

accepted_gaps.title: Equity and observability
accepted_gaps.statement: Data scarcity and research-effort bias can distort risk ranks and resource allocation.

rejected_gaps.title: Humans only need a larger universal model
rejected_gaps.reason: The evidence instead points to target definition, data quality, validation, and governance constraints.
